reference: Bash type/help verify metadata. Offline operation contracts use hand-encoded RFC 1035 zone/message fixtures and the documented chain/checkzone/doh-codec output API. No network or GNU dig/drill equivalence is claimed.
coverage: Bash builtin classification for the statically installed dns loadable.
Short description, synopsis, and documented command-family metadata exposed by Bash help.
Deferred operation coverage is scoped to DNS query transports, client updates, and local resolver/authoritative service exchanges.
Offline parent-chain calculation, valid/inherited-owner and invalid-address master-file parsing, and a fixed in-memory DoH POST decoder contract.
exclusions: All network exchanges, listener/service operations, transfers and polling remain deferred; offline parser/codec cases do not establish network parity.
Signing, credentials and trust-anchor management are unexecuted. Broader offline parser/codec conformance remains a gap.

cases.purpose: GNU Bash type -t reports a loaded Bash builtin as builtin. This confirms availability metadata without invoking dns.
Bash help -d exposes the documented DNS command description; metadata only.
Bash help -s exposes the documented public query synopsis; metadata only.
cases.stdout: dns: dns A|AAAA|MX|TXT|... HOST [-s SERVER] [-t TIMEOUT_MS] [-d] [--validate] [--skew SEC]

cases.purpose: The complete help text retains stable documentation for the master-file checker, authoritative server, and DNSSEC features; checks only Bash metadata and does not run those commands.
Exercise DNS query construction, response parsing, common RR presentation, error responses, resolver search order, and TC-triggered TCP fallback.
cases.reason: Requires a controlled UDP DNS responder and TCP fallback peer to exchange packets. Network activity is outside this task's allowed execution. A future disposable VM must bind only private loopback fixtures, record request bytes, and compare response parsing against RFC 1035 encodings and normalized dig/drill output; include A, AAAA, MX, TXT, PTR, NXDOMAIN, malformed response, and truncation cases.

cases.purpose: Exercise DNS-over-TLS and DNS-over-HTTPS framing, certificate validation, and DNS message handling through each transport.
cases.reason: Requires TLS and HTTPS peers plus certificate fixtures or the documented BASHDNS_DOT_CMD/BASHDNS_DOH_CMD transport seams. This task forbids network activity. A future disposable VM must use loopback-only mock peers, a private test CA, fixed DNS wire replies, and byte-level TLS/HTTP framing assertions.

cases.purpose: Exercise RFC 2136 update and RFC 1996 notify requests, prerequisite encodings, TSIG signing, and peer response validation.
cases.reason: These client operations send DNS packets and need a controlled authoritative peer. A future disposable VM must provide loopback UDP/TCP responders and compare the requests with independently encoded RFC 2136/RFC 1996 messages and HMAC-SHA256 TSIG calculations. No packets are sent in this suite.

cases.purpose: Exercise authoritative UDP/TCP answers, zone selection, transfer/update policy, TSIG, and opt-in service features against clients.
cases.reason: The auth-serve subcommand opens a network listener and requires client exchanges. A future disposable VM must isolate the listener to loopback, provide deterministic zone fixtures and independent DNS packet encoders, and verify answers, denied/allowed transfer behavior, and permitted update behavior without contacting any external peer.

cases.purpose: Exercise resolver forwarding/cache behavior and the documented recursive, DNSSEC, DNS64, and policy paths against controlled peers.
cases.reason: The resolver service exchanges DNS packets with clients and upstreams. A future disposable VM must use a loopback client and scripted upstream server, fixed time and zone data, and independent DNSSEC/DNS64 expectations. This suite performs no network activity.

cases.purpose: Exercise slave IXFR/AXFR transfer verification and DNSKEY polling used by trust-anchor rollover.
cases.reason: Transfer and polling paths require a controlled DNS primary and response stream. A future disposable VM must expose only a loopback primary with fixed signed zone/DNSKEY fixtures, injected timestamps, and independently computed TSIG/signature expectations. No transfer or poll is run here.

cases.purpose: Compute the documented parent-domain chain as a pure text operation without DNS resolution.
Validate a small RFC 1035 zone including an inherited owner and documented serial reporting; addresses are text only.
cases.script:
cat > zone <<'ZONE'
$ORIGIN example.test.
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns.example.test. hostmaster.example.test. 2026010101 3600 600 86400 300
@ IN NS ns.example.test.
ns IN A 192.0.2.1
www IN A 192.0.2.2
    IN AAAA 2001:db8::2
ZONE
dns checkzone -o example.test. zone

cases.purpose: Reject an ordinary malformed address in a private master file without opening sockets.
cases.script:
cat > zone <<'ZONE'
$ORIGIN example.test.
$TTL 300
@ IN SOA ns.example.test. hostmaster.example.test. 2026010101 3600 600 86400 300
@ IN NS ns.example.test.
ns IN A 192.0.2.1
www IN A 192.0.2.999
    IN AAAA 2001:db8::2
ZONE
dns checkzone -o example.test. zone

cases.purpose: Decode an independently encoded twelve-byte DNS message from an HTTP POST body; the codec is a pure memory interface, with no peer or socket.
